messages:
alex: paging SRE — urgent: trying to push hotfix but CI failing across the board. github actions returning 503s when contacting npm.pkg.github.com and auth token errors. hotfix deploy is blocked. :rotating_light:
maya: oncall here, I'm looking. can you paste the CI failure output?
jordan: saw similar alerts in our CI fleet — runners are timing out pulling packages from github packages. grabbing logs now.
alex: paste from one job:
```
npm ERR! code E503
npm ERR! response 503 Service Unavailable
npm ERR! request to https://npm.pkg.github.com/@redwood/inference-cli/-/inference-cli-1.2.3.tgz failed, reason: connect ECONNRESET
```
maya: ok, thanks. checked https://www.githubstatus.com/ shows "Partial Outage: GitHub Packages (npm) — Investigating". ticket opened 4608672 by incident-bot.
incident-bot: Incident created: GH Packages partial outage (4608672). Severity: Major. Pager escalations sent.
npm packages are central to the hotfix pipeline here — build step `npm ci` is blocked.
sophie: what's the customer impact right now? any customer-facing features broken?
alex: hotfix is for model-serving config exploit patch; canary not yet rolled out. No live regressions reported but we need to ship ASAP for customers on Dedicated.
npm: we rely on github packages for private npm org packages; we do have S3-based cache for public deps only. devex could try to publish a tarball to S3 and point CI at it as a workaround.
tariq: I can spin up a temporary artifact mirror. I have an infra script to push the built tarball to our internal S3 bucket and update build matrix to install from URL. Will need someone to build the artifact locally and upload.
lina: support here — prepping status page message if we can't ship within 2 hours. need ETA from eng.
maya: handoff: I'm going offline for 30m to triage infra alerts, jordan you're the secondary oncall after my block. jordan?
jordan: taking. pairing with alex to get a local build. alex, can you try `npm pack` locally and upload artifact to s3://redwood-temp-artifacts/hotfix-1.2.3.tgz?
alex: working on it now. local `npm pack` produced inference-cli-1.2.3.tgz. uploading...
```
aws s3 cp inference-cli-1.2.3.tgz s3://redwood-temp-artifacts/ --acl private
```
alex: upload complete. public link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp-artifacts/inference-cli-1.2.3.tgz (internal perms).
tariq: updated CI matrix to use `npm install https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp-artifacts/inference-cli-1.2.3.tgz` for the build job. kicking off a run.
deploy-bot: CI run started (#2109) — runner pool: gha-eu-1.

jordan: CI runner started but node is failing early with auth to GH API for actions artifacts: separate issue? logs show 401 on api.github.com when trying to fetch action inputs. need to confirm if it's an auth token rate-limit or broader outage.

alex: logs:
```
GET https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/inference/actions/artifacts 401 Unauthorized
auth error: token rejected: message="Bad credentials"
```

maya: that smells like the GHA runtime tokens are failing or GitHub is returning 401s while packages are 503. GitHub status also listing increased API error rates. I'm opening a support escalation link with GH support and linking our incident.

pm-aaron: for customer comms: can we be precise — "builds and deploys may be delayed due to third-party GitHub Packages and Actions service degradation" — also note which customers (Dedicated) might see delayed rollouts.

lina: drafting status message now, adding note about active mitigation (artifact mirror + manual build) and that we are investigating root cause with GitHub. will post in 15 if no change.

sophie: alternatives: 1) manual deploy of hotfix via direct docker image (if we can build locally and push to registry), 2) rollback config to old release to avoid needing new artifact, 3) use internal mirror as we are doing. pros/cons?

jordan: manual docker build works if we can get the binary — we can `npm pack` -> build image locally on bastion and push to our docker registry (we control that). this bypasses GH packages and actions entirely for release. I'll coordinate with infra for docker creds.

alex: local docker build succeeded. pushed to docker.redwood.internal:5000/hotfix:1.2.3. triggering canary deploy via our console API now.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment initiated for service model-serving-hotfix -> version hotfix:1.2.3. Canary size: 5%.

maya: noted. handoff complete: I'm back to monitoring; jordan you remain leading the mitigation. I'll stay looped.

jordan: monitoring canary logs — initial requests look okay, latency normal. no errors in first 2000 requests.

pm-aaron: calling out to account owners for Dedicated customers with active rollouts to make them aware of possible delays. cc: @sales.

lina: status posted: "Partial outage with GitHub Actions and GitHub Packages affecting builds/deploys. We are mitigating by publishing artifacts to an internal mirror and performing manual canary deployments. No customer request failures observed at this time; Dedicated deployments may be delayed. Updates every 30 minutes." :writing_hand:

incident-bot: GitHub support case 4608672 updated — GH acknowledged degraded performance in Packages and Actions; ETA unknown.

sophie: next steps: document the workaround steps (npm pack -> s3 upload -> update CI matrix) in runbook, add a checklist to avoid repeating manual steps, and evaluate adding automatic fallback to internal artifact mirror for critical pipelines. tariq, can you capture that in a PR to infra repo?

tariq: yes, creating PR with script + example matrix snippet. tagging devex for review.

alex: postmortem notes for incident timeline and impact: root cause external (GitHub), mitigation: internal artifact mirror and manual docker push, customer impact: potential delay for Dedicated rollouts but no customer-facing errors observed, time to mitigated canary: ~40m.

maya: thanks all. closing the immediate page once canary reaches 30% and metrics steady. will escalate if GH status changes. :white_check_mark:

pm-aaron: adding note to customer comms requesting permission to share GH incident link.

lina: final status update posted: "Mitigation in place; canary rolling out via internal artifacts. Monitoring."
